_comment: Shared vectors for the rubber band of a Drawer panel dragged past its dock.
Read by coui_core (CoreDrawerRubberBand, CoreCubicBezier.transform), coui_flutter (real drags on
all four sides, the sheet and the backdrop variants), coui_web (the markup the entry emits, and the
same arithmetic) and a real-Chrome probe of the Web drawer, so a rule that changes on one platform
fails on the others. Computed outside Dart, so the table is the oracle rather than a copy of the code.
UNITS. Distances are logical pixels. A PULL is how far the pointer has carried the panel along its
slide axis, signed by the edge the panel hides behind: positive toward that edge, negative toward the
viewport centre (further open than fully open). Times are milliseconds.
constants: the Core defaults the rows are computed with (reach is a fraction of the panel extent).
stretch.cases: overshoot is how far past the dock the pointer is (px); extent is the panel's length
on its slide axis; stretch is how far the far edge has moved out (the docked edge never moves);
scale is (extent + stretch) / extent, the scale about the docked edge.
pose.cases: the pose for a pull. slide is the distance moved toward the hiding edge, stretch the
distance the far edge has moved out; at most one is non-zero.
inverse.cases: overshootOf(stretch, extent).
settle: a displacement of `from` px on its way back to the dock. offset is what is left atMs after
the release: from * (1 - easing(atMs / durationMs)). The same curve is a CSS cubic-bezier on the Web
and a Cubic on Flutter, so the samples are what a browser and a framework both have to draw.
gestures: a drag on a panel `extent` px long. steps are the pulls the pointer passes through, one
move each, over durationMs at constant pace; holdMs, when present, is a rest before the lift.
pose is where the panel is drawn at the last step. dismisses is what the release does. settle, when
present, is the displacement left atMs after a release that did not dismiss. The speeds keep a wide
margin either side of the 400 px/s a flick needs: a probe on a loaded machine delivers its events
late, which can only make a flick slower.
